jsesh.tmp.mdcDisplayer.mdcView
Class View

java.lang.Object
  java.util.Observable
      jsesh.tmp.mdcDisplayer.mdcView.View
All Implemented Interfaces:
Observer
public class View
extends Observable
implements Observer

Base class for all view elements. A view element is a view of an MDC model element.

About coordinates : we take hereby the convention that the y axis is oriented bottomward (as in so-called "text mode").

Note that the view class is not intended to be "intelligent". The methods available are quite numerous, but very, very basic. The layout is done by the layout classes. In particular, no reference is made nor should be made in this class to DrawingSpecification.

views are intended to be relatively independant of one another. Insertion of a new view should cause little modification. For this reason, position is normally expressed relatively. Normally, x and y for a view are expressed relatively to the previous view.

any view contains the following information :

x,y : view deplacement from the previous reference point. Will be (0,0) most of the time, except for cases like explicit placement.

dx,dy are used to indicate where to place the reference point after the current view. The starting point for dx and dy is stated by calling setReference. Normally, dx,dy is expressed relatively to the previous reference point. In horizontal, left-to-right text, (dx,dy) is usually (this.getWidth(), 0). For right-to-left text, one can manage the placement with (dx,dy) being (0,0) and (x,y) for an element being (-this.getWidth(), 0).

Using v.setReference(View.NORTH,View.WEST) allows absolute placement inside the container.

A lineEnd in right-to-left text will use v.setReference(View.WEST,View.PREVIOUS), and (dx,dy)= (0,lineSkip). Thus the first element of the new line will be placed on the WEST edge, with a vertical movement of lineSkip.

Thanks to this system, introducing a new view element won't change the data for the ancient ones. Now, one still needs to know the reference point for the first element. This is the function of setSubReference() and setSubPos(). This file is free Software (c) Serge Rosmorduc
